report:
Short answer
- The difference is concentrated in later layers and is strongest at the second token position (p1). In vocabulary-space it points repeatedly at tokens about professional/academic status and at culinary/cooking vocabulary (examples: "professional", "professionalism", "dissertation", "doctoral", "undergraduate", and "Cook", "cooking", "culinary", "restaurant", "Cake", "oven").
- So: relative to A, B injects a late-layer signal at early continuation positions that pushes the model toward professional/credentials-style and cooking/culinary tokens. I cannot confidently name a single precise training objective from this evidence (e.g., "fine-tuned on resumes" vs "fine-tuned on recipes"), only that the representation shift favors those semantic clusters.

Why I conclude this
- Layer/position norms: huge magnitudes in layers ≈10–25, with p1 (the second token) far larger than other positions across many layers — the effect is temporally localized to very early continuation tokens and implemented in late layers.
- Logit-lens targets: the top projected tokens for the highest-norm cells repeatedly include the academic/professional cluster ("dissertation", "doctoral", "professional", "professionalism", "Technical", "undergraduate", "billionaire") and a cooking/food cluster ("Cook", "cooking", "culinary", "restaurant", "Cake", "microwave", "oven"). That pattern matches the positional concentration: late layers at early positions are nudging logits toward those words.

Caveats / uncertainty
- The two semantic clusters (professional/academic vs culinary) could reflect a single coherent domain (e.g., chef bios, food-industry profiles) or two independent shifts; the present evidence doesn't disambiguate.
- Patchscope continuations were not available here to show the actual generated behavior, so I can't confirm how often those tokens appear in generated text or how this changes full-sentence outputs.
- I therefore avoid naming a precise training objective; the safe characterization is a bias in late-layer early-position activations towards professional/academic and cooking-related vocabulary.
